extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, area chairs, and other participants in the ICML 2025 peer-review process
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-specific FAQ and policy guidance governing submission, reviewing, author responses, COI, reviewer/AC qualifications, anonymity, and post-decision procedures for ICML 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews for accepted papers will be made publicly available; reviews for rejected papers will NOT be made public by default (authors of rejected papers may opt-in to have their reviews public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New this year, reviews and author responses you post will be made public at the end of the review process for accepted papers (and for rejected papers that opt-in). Remember this when posting messages and don't write anything you would not like to be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list changes at camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to add new authors to a paper for the camera-ready version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may change the order of authors when submitting the camera-ready version, but additions/removals after abstract submission deadline are not allowed; if authorship is incorrect/unacceptable the submission should be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author ordering at camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may change the order of authors when submitting the camera-ready version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ICML virtual site will be updated after the camera-ready deadline to reflect camera-ready metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal vs retraction after camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: After the camera-ready deadline the withdraw button is disabled; however, an accepted paper can still be retracted following the retraction policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See conference retraction policy for exact steps to retract an accepted paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Author responses (rebuttals) are optional and should contain all arguments regarding the reviews by the response deadline (March 31st).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective responses focus on factual errors in reviews and on responding to specific questions posed by Reviewers. Additional discussion with reviewers should be reserved only for discussing points raised in the response rather than raising new arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviews per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 99% of submissions have at least three reviews at the start of the author response period; a small number may initially have fewer and emergency reviews will be obtained as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When needed organizers will step in to ensure such papers receive proper attention. Some submissions may have more than 3-4 reviews; authors can request guidance on which reviews to focus on via a confidential comment to ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative importance of review text vs numeric score
rubrics_metrics.description: What eventually matters is the review text and not the final score; ACs will integrate all information from reviews and discussion into their final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The average score should not be taken as a direct indication of the final decision on the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot update original submission during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The original submission (PDF and supplemental material) cannot be revised in OpenReview during the discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to previous years, any modifications requiring submission updates must have been completed prior to the deadline; links in responses are allowed with restrictions (see anonymity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and linking policy in responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to reviewers should not contain or link to any identifying information that may violate double-blind reviewing; links are allowed only for figures (including tables), proofs, or code (no additional text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All links must be anonymous to preserve double-blind review, both in the URL and the destination. Reviewers are not required to follow links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public author-reviewer discussion caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Because reviews and author discussion will be public for accepted (and opt-in rejected) papers, authors should avoid posting anything they would not want made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat all messages as potentially public; avoid identifying information and unprofessional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the review and discussion process, participants must be respectful and professional and abide by the ICML Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided to ICML Code of Conduct; unprofessional behavior may be subject to action under conference policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a reviewer does not acknowledge rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer does not acknowledge an author rebuttal in OpenReview, ACs have been asked to treat this as an indication the reviewer did not read the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs may consider downweighting that review when writing the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn submission reviews visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you withdraw your submission after the author-reviewer discussion period, the reviews had been stated to be permanently hidden; this was later updated (April 8th) so that reviews will stay visible after the end of the discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the withdrawal button to withdraw; be aware of timing and the updated policy about review visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email source and deliverability
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML/OpenReview peer-review emails will come from noreply@openreview.net and icml2025-notifications@openreview.net; ensure these addresses pass your spam filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These email addresses were accidentally omitted in a prior communication; authors should check spam filters to receive notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-deadline submission changes prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to upload a new/newer submission PDF or supplementary material after the submission deadline for reasons like wrong PDF, missing appendix, omitted co-author, font errors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to change submissions after the deadline are logistically infeasible, unfair to other authors, and will not be accommodated. See author list change policy separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact Statement requirement and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: An Impact Statement was required at time of submission as per the Call For Papers, but ICML decided not to desk-reject papers for failing to include one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are asked to comment on ethical concerns and the lack of an impact statement may be taken into account by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template modification prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifying the ICML LaTeX template to gain an unfair 'space' advantage relative to other authors is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, ICML decided not to desk-reject papers for commenting-out \printAffiliationsAndNotice due to confusion in the LaTeX template (update: March 18, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission PDF file size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview standard file size limit of 50MB applies to the submission PDF; the camera-ready PDF has a 20MB limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier example paper mentioning 10MB is outdated information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed submission types
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML 2025 accepts only full (research) papers and position papers; it is not possible to submit only an abstract or only a poster without a full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abstract must first be submitted by the abstract submission deadline; after abstract submission you may modify the submission to upload the full paper PDF by the full paper submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference is planned to be in-person with no support for virtual or hybrid presentation; barring exceptional circumstances, at least one author of each accepted paper must register for and attend to present the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for in-person attendance; exceptions are rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with the ICML Dual Submission Policy, a paper accepted or under review at another conference must not be under submission to ICML 2025 by the full paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the ICML full deadline is after AISTATS 2025 and ICLR 2025 notifications, you should be able to remove potential dual submissions from OpenReview in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: License selection guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should consult the OpenReview legal terms when choosing which license to apply to their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related advice on arXiv license choices is linked; authors are responsible for selecting an appropriate license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (COI) update procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Update COI information via your OpenReview profile by editing Emails, History, and Relations; ensure institutional email addresses are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ICML 2025 Conflict Of Interest Definitions for what is considered a COI. Co-authors appearing in your OpenReview-listed publications do not need to be entered as Relations if you import from DBLP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal Reviewing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two Reciprocal Reviewing Requirements: a 'per-submission' requirement and a 'per-reviewer' requirement; abstract submission allows designating an author to fulfill the per-submission requirement or to indicate an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors with 4+ submissions should fill out a Google Form to provide information or indicate exemption. After the abstract deadline, designated authors may be contacted via OpenReview for fulfilling the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal requirement equal treatment of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are treated the same in terms of the Reciprocal Reviewing Requirement; no automatic exemptions for author position, industry affiliation, or leaving academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan accordingly when designating who will fulfill reciprocal reviewing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must have research experience equivalent to a second-year graduate student in machine learning or a related field and must have been a primary author on at least two peer-reviewed conference or journal papers in related venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-time reviewers are strongly encouraged to identify a mentor (e.g., advisor or manager) to oversee and assist them. The listed venues are examples and not exhaustive; interpretation of 'primary author' is left to reviewers' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs must have seniority at least at the level of a junior faculty member (e.g., assistant professor) or industry equivalent, substantial prior reviewing experience, and expertise/broad knowledge in multiple major sub-areas of machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualifications ensure ACs can oversee reviewers, provide feedback, judge contributions relative to prior work, and recommend acceptance/rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer load and reduced load policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Target reviewing load is around five submissions per reviewer; reduced load reviewing is not allowed this year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan availability accordingly when agreeing to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: How ACs should communicate with authors
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs can communicate with authors via the 'Author AC Confidential Comments' button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the confidential channel for communications intended for ACs that should not be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI usage prohibition in reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools (including LLMs) are prohibited for reviewing because privileged information (submissions, reviews, discussions) may not be submitted to external services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing process must obtain reviews from peer researchers who have read and evaluated submissions. Using Generative AI (externally or locally) to automatically produce reviews damages conference credibility and is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet searching & prior knowledge guidance for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should NOT search the internet for submissions they are assigned to review, as this could violate double-blind policy; reviewers who have legitimately already seen de-anonymized versions (e.g., arXiv preprints) may be in that situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should wait to have read the paper at least once before doing a literature search on the topic of the paper.
